Clause Part 1 - environmental_protection (environmental_protection): Residential Development 
Building designs for new houses, alterations to houses, dual occupancies and residential flat buildings are required to comply with the BASIX State Environmental Planning Policy (SEPP). 
Council is unable to approve a development application for residential development that does not achieve the minimum BASIX ratings. BASIX sets out requirements on how to achieve water conservation and energy efficiency targets for residential development.

Clause Part 1 - development_control (development_control): A BASIX certificate is required to be submitted to Council with each development application and this certificate certifies that the dwelling proposal will meet the required environmental targets.

Clause Part 1 - environmental_protection (environmental_protection): The Building Code of Australia (BCA) requires certain non-residential building types to demonstrate they will meet minimum criteria for reducing energy consumption. This compliance must be shown at Construction Certificate stage. It affects what are defined in the BCA as Class 5 to 9 building types (e.g. office buildings, restaurants, shops and schools).

Clause Part 1 - environmental_protection (environmental_protection): Alterations and additions to existing buildings, when the extent of work exceeds 50 percent of the existing building area, are also affected.

Clause Part 1 - development_control (development_control): In order to comply with the BCA energy requirements at the Construction Certificate stage, the design of new buildings will have to be resolved “upfront” at development application stage. This is fundamental for arriving at an acceptable design, as environmental design cannot be an afterthought at the Construction Certificate stage.

Clause Part 1 - environmental_protection (environmental_protection): Inner West Council encourages applicants to go beyond the requirements of BASIX, and to incorporate as many sustainable design principles as possible
